cleanIntro: The Tactical is the 509 FN drew this book around — the nomenclature figures are captioned as the Tactical, with a threaded barrel cap at the muzzle and MRD screws on the slide. That changes the order of the strip rather than the strip itself: the muzzle device comes off before the takedown lever moves, and the optic stays put unless you are cleaning under it.

steps.title: Confirm it says 509, and note that the Tactical is the pistol drawn here
steps.action: Read the designation on the slide. The pistol illustrated throughout this manual is the 509 Tactical, so the figures should match what is in your hand — a longer threaded muzzle, taller sights, an optics cut on the slide. If your pistol has no 509 in its name, get FN's book for it instead.
steps.prose: That the Tactical is the drawn pistol is useful and slightly misleading at once: the figures show a threaded barrel cap and MRD screws, but FN writes the procedures for the whole 509 series and qualifies the threaded-barrel and manual-safety sections as optional. The specification table gives the Tactical its own column — 4.5-inch barrel, 7.9 inches overall, 27.9 ounces, standard magazines of 24 and 17 — which is a longer slide and barrel than the plain 509, and the reason a suppressor host handles differently on the bench.
steps.aside: IF YOUR FN PISTOL DOES NOT HAVE 509 IN ITS NAMING CONVENTION OR IF THE APPEARANCE OF THE PISTOL DOES NOT CORRESPOND TO THE ILLUSTRATIONS IN THIS OWNER’S MANUAL CONTACT YOUR DEALER, DEPARTMENT ARMORER OR CONTACT FN DIRECTLY TO OBTAIN THE OWNER’S MANUAL THAT HAS BEEN WRITTEN SPECIFICALLY FOR YOUR PISTOL.
steps.quote: Right view of the FN 509 Tactical pistol (non-manual safety model shown).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §5 Nomenclature, figure caption, p.14

steps.title: Magazine out — and the Tactical's standard one is 24 rounds
steps.action: Muzzle safe, finger off the trigger, press the magazine release and take the magazine out. If it hangs up, pull on the base plate while holding the release in.
steps.prose: A 24-round 509 Tactical magazine is long, heavy and sits proud of the grip, so it is the one most likely to stay put in a fouled magazine well and the one most worth catching rather than dropping on concrete. The release is guarded against being pressed by a drop or against a flat surface, which means it wants a deliberate press with the pad of the thumb. Set the magazine well away from the bench before the slide moves.
steps.quote: Press the magazine release and remove the magazine. If the magazine does not drop out of the pistol, pull on the magazine base plate while pressing the magazine release (Figure 12).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §6.3 Unloading, step 1, p.22
steps.warn: Magazine first, always. Racking the slide with a loaded magazine still in the Tactical chambers a fresh round rather than clearing one.

steps.title: Eject the chambered round and lock the slide open
steps.action: Pull the slide fully rearward to throw out any chambered round, then press the slide stop up and let the slide rest back against it.
steps.prose: The Tactical's slide is longer and its serrations are the same, so it is no harder to run — but the extra mass means a half-hearted pull is even more likely to strip a round part way and drop it back. One firm stroke, all the way. If a can is fitted, take it off before you start racking; a heavy muzzle device changes how the slide feels and can mask a round that has not actually cleared.
steps.quote: Lock the slide to the rear by pressing the slide stop up and allowing the slide to rest against the slide stop retaining it to the rear (Figure 13).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §6.3 Unloading, step 2, p.22

steps.title: Eyes in the chamber and the magazine well
steps.action: With the slide locked open, look into the ejection port at the chamber and down into the magazine well and confirm both are empty.
steps.prose: On a Tactical wearing an optic the sight body sits over the rear of the slide and can shade the ejection port — move the pistol into the light rather than squinting past the mount. The extractor's red dot behind the port tells you when a case is present but is not evidence of empty. Later in this strip the trigger gets pressed deliberately, so this look is what makes that safe.
steps.quote: Inspect the chamber and magazine well to ensure no cartridge is present. Remember, merely removing the magazine does not mean the chamber is unloaded (Figure 14).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §6.3 Unloading, step 3, p.22
steps.warn: THE RED DOT THAT INDICATES A LOADED CHAMBER CAN BECOME OBSCURED. DO NOT DEPEND ON THE RED INDICATOR TO DETERMINE THE UNLOADED CONDITION OF THE PISTOL.

steps.title: Manual safety or not — the Tactical is sold both ways
steps.action: Check the rear of the frame above the grip for a small lever on each side. If your Tactical has them, push them down to the fire position before disassembly. If it does not, this pistol has no manual safety and nothing here applies.
steps.prose: FN's own figure caption for the Tactical says "non-manual safety model shown", which is the clearest possible statement that both exist and the drawing is only one of them. It matters because the safety blocks the sear carrier and trigger assembly, and this strip includes a trigger press to drop the striker — with the levers up, nothing releases and the slide will not come forward off the frame. FN also notes the safety cannot be engaged once the trigger is back, so do not reach for it partway through.
steps.quote: 9.2 MANUAL SAFETY (APPLICABLE ONLY TO PISTOLS WITH A MANUAL SAFETY)
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §9.2 heading, p.30

steps.title: Muzzle device or thread protector off first
steps.action: Unscrew the thread protector — or the suppressor, compensator or other muzzle device — counterclockwise off the ½"-28 threads and put it aside before touching the takedown lever.
steps.prose: On the Tactical this is not the optional step it is on a plain 509: the threaded barrel is what the model is for, and the nomenclature figure shows the cap fitted. Take it off first because it hangs in front of the slide and gets in the way when the slide runs forward off the frame, and because the threads and the last quarter inch of bore are where suppressed fouling concentrates. FN wants the protector back on whenever no device is fitted, so keep track of it.
steps.aside: FN's qualifier on that section: 9.8 THREADED BARREL (APPLICABLE ONLY TO PISTOLS WITH THREADED BARRELS).
steps.quote: The threading is ½" -28 and comes with a thread protector that should be installed if a suppressor or muzzle device is not installed (Figure 35).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §9.8 Threaded barrel, p.34

steps.title: Takedown lever, 100 degrees clockwise
steps.action: With the slide still locked to the rear, rotate the takedown lever about 100 degrees clockwise until it stops.
steps.prose: A hundred degrees, not ninety — it goes past square and stops with a positive feel, and a lever left short is why a slide then refuses to come off. The slide must stay locked open for the lever to clear; if it has crept forward, put it back on the slide stop rather than levering harder. On a suppressor-height setup with an optic aboard, brace the pistol against the bench so the extra weight up top does not twist it out of your grip while you turn the lever.
steps.quote: Rotate the takedown lever approximately 100 deg. clockwise (Figure 41).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.1 Field strip, step 4, p.36

steps.title: Drop the striker with slide and frame in line
steps.action: Hold the slide, release it off the slide stop and ease it forward under control. Keep the rear of the slide aligned with the rear of the frame, point the muzzle safely, and press the trigger to release the striker.
steps.prose: FN's own warning for this step is that the pistol must be completely unloaded to do it, which is why the chamber was checked by eye. Alignment is the trick: let the slide run right forward and the sear picks the striker up again, and you will be pulling on a slide that will not release. If it recocks, bring it back into line and press once more — never try to force a slide off a cocked striker.
steps.quote: While keeping the rear of the slide and rear of the frame in alignment, point the muzzle in a safe direction and press the trigger to release the striker. The slide will move forward slightly when released (Figure 43).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.1 Field strip, step 5, p.37
steps.warn: THE PISTOL MUST BE COMPLETELY UNLOADED TO PERFORM STEP 5. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THIS WARNING COULD RESULT IN SERIOUS INJURY OR DEATH.

steps.title: Slide assembly forward off the frame
steps.action: With the striker down, run the slide forward and lift it clear of the frame rails, barrel and recoil spring still inside.
steps.prose: It should come away with no force. A Tactical with an optic mounted is top-heavy and awkward at this moment, so take the weight with a full hand rather than pinching the serrations, and do not put it down optic-first. If it binds, the striker has recocked or the lever has moved back — reset instead of pulling.
steps.quote: After releasing the striker, you can remove the slide by pulling the slide forward and away from the frame.
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.1 Field strip, step 6, p.37

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly out by its small forward spring
steps.action: Turn the slide upside down, grasp the small spring at the front of the recoil spring assembly, lift that end out of its recess and draw the assembly out.
steps.prose: The Tactical's longer slide takes the same captive assembly geometry — seated in a recess at the front of the slide, its rear centred on the barrel lug. Lift by the small forward spring so you are releasing the compression, not fighting it. It stays assembled: a guide rod separated from its springs is a service item, not a cleaning task.
steps.quote: Hold the slide upside down, grasp the small spring of the recoil spring assembly then lift the recoil spring assembly up and out of the slide (Figure 45).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.1 Field strip, step 7, p.38

steps.title: Barrel up, around the extractor, then rearward out
steps.action: Grip the 4.5-inch barrel by its lug, lift it up, take it around the extractor and slide it rearward out of the slide.
steps.prose: Three motions and they have to happen in that order — lift to clear the lug, swing around the extractor claw rather than into it, then back out the breech end. Forcing a threaded barrel straight back is worse than on the plain gun because the muzzle end is longer and gives you more leverage against the extractor. With the barrel out, the threads at the muzzle are finally accessible for a brush.
steps.quote: Grasp the barrel by its lug, lift it up and around the extractor and slide the barrel rearward out of the slide (Figure 46).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.1 Field strip, step 9, p.38

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, 4.5-inch threaded barrel, recoil spring assembly, plus the thread protector or muzzle device. FN calls that sufficient for a thorough clean and puts anything further in an armorer's hands.
steps.prose: That gives you the bore from the chamber end, the muzzle threads, the breech face and extractor, both slide rails, the barrel unlock surface and the magazine well. A Tactical run suppressed fouls faster than a plain 509 — FN names suppressor use alongside dirty ammunition as a reason to clean more often, and the 500-round interval for intensive shooting is a ceiling, not a target. Deep Clean covers the magazine, the backstrap, the optics plate and the muzzle device itself.
steps.quote: This level of disassembly is sufficient to perform a thorough cleaning. Disassembly beyond the instructions provided in this manual should only be carried out by a qualified armorer.
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.1 Field strip, closing note, p.38

deepSteps.title: The muzzle device: caliber rating, thread pattern, bore alignment
deepSteps.action: With the device off, clean its threads and shoulder, then before it goes back check it is rated for the caliber marked on the back of the barrel, that it carries ½"-28 right-hand threads, and that its bore lines up with the barrel's with nothing obstructing the bullet.
deepSteps.prose: This is the step where a Tactical can be destroyed by a part that fits. FN devotes most of §11.6 to the two ways it goes wrong — a device bored for a smaller caliber, or one threaded on out of square — and both wreck the device and the pistol together. Thread it on square by hand first and only then torque it to the maker's figure; if it starts to cross-thread, back it all the way off rather than working through it.
deepSteps.quote: FN 509 pistols with threaded barrels are threaded with ½"- 28 right-hand threads and allow the pistol to be equipped with a suppressor or muzzle device.
deepSteps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.6 Suppressor and muzzle device installation and use, p.48
deepSteps.warn: FN also notes that a suppressor attached without a Nielsen device will fire safely but will not cycle the pistol properly — so a Tactical that short-strokes after a clean is often telling you about the mount, not the gun.

deepSteps.title: Under the optic: screws dry, o-ring seated, no threadlocker
deepSteps.action: If you are cleaning under the optic or the slide cap, back both screws out counterclockwise, lift off the optic, the MRD plate and the o-ring, and clean the mounting cut. Refit with all lubricant removed from the screws and their holes, the o-ring in its recess, the plate sandwiching it, and the screws tightened by finger pressure with the T10 Torx.
deepSteps.prose: FN's low-profile system is self-locking, and adding threadlocker can seize the screws so hard the optic cannot come off again without damage. The opposite mistake matters just as much on a Tactical, which is a pistol people actually shoot suppressed: oil in the screw holes lets the fasteners walk under recoil and the zero goes with them. Zeroing has to be confirmed every time the optic comes off, so treat this as a job with a range trip attached.
deepSteps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.5 Optics mounting system, note, p.47

deepSteps.title: Magazine apart — cap the spring before the plate moves
deepSteps.action: Empty the magazine. Point the base away from you, press the floor plate catch through the hole in the floor plate, slide the plate forward off the body with your hand over the spring, then remove the catch, spring and follower.
deepSteps.prose: The 24-round Tactical magazine has the longest spring in the family and it is under real tension at the floor plate — let the plate jump and the catch goes across the room. Palm over the base, plate forward, then bleed the pressure off slowly. Rebuilding, match the follower's angle to the feed lips and confirm the catch tab is standing proud through the floor plate before the magazine goes back in the pistol.
deepSteps.aside: FN's own limit on which magazines this book covers: FN 509 magazines not specifically covered in this manual should be covered by an addendum included with this manual or with the magazine.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the floor plate catch, magazine spring and follower from the magazine body (Figure 60).
deepSteps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.4 Magazine disassembly, step 2, p.43
deepSteps.warn: CAUTION: THE MAGAZINE SPRING IS UNDER TENSION. WEAR EYE PROTECTION AND KEEP THE BOTTOM OF THE MAGAZINE POINTED IN A SAFE DIRECTION.

deepSteps.title: Backstrap off with a 5/64" roll pin punch
deepSteps.action: With the frame stripped and empty, drive the backstrap retaining pin out using a small 5/64" roll pin punch, then slide the backstrap down off the dovetail.
deepSteps.prose: It is a roll pin — a solid punch or a nail crushes it and then the backstrap will not stay put. Taking it off exposes the grip channel underneath, which never sees a brush otherwise and which collects sweat and lint on a duty pistol. Going back on, close the gap at the top of the backstrap and align its pin hole with the dovetail slot before the pin starts.
deepSteps.quote: Using a small 5/64" roll pin punch, push out the backstrap
deepSteps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.3 Backstrap removal, step 1, p.41

cleaning.name: BARREL, BORE & MUZZLE THREADS
tasks: Solvent into the bore and chamber, a few minutes to work, then rod and patches from the chamber end only — never from the muzzle
Brush the ½"-28 threads and the shoulder behind them; that is where suppressor carbon builds and where a device starts to sit crooked
Patch until clean, then one patch with preservative oil through the bore to protect it
Light oil on the outside of the barrel and its unlock surface

cleaning.name: SLIDE, OPTIC CUT & FRAME
tasks: Breech face, under the extractor and around the ejection port with a brush and solvent — a suppressed Tactical blows more residue back through the port than a plain gun
Both slide rails wiped and given a drop of lightweight oil, along with the striker block, sear, disconnect cam, cartridge guide and unlock block FN's lubrication figure names
If the optic is off, clean the mounting cut and the screw holes dry — no oil in the threads
Soft cloth through the magazine well; keep solvent away from the polymer frame

cleaning.name: INTERVAL & PUT-AWAY
tasks: Never soak the pistol; go sparing with lubricant, because FN warns excess interferes with function
Clean after every use, and at latest every 500 rounds in intensive shooting — sooner again if it has been run suppressed
Wipe the exterior free of dirt, fingerprints and excess oil before storage
Dry-patch the bore before shooting so storage oil is not in front of the first round

reassembly: Barrel into the slide: muzzle through the barrel hole from the inside, drop it down, slide it back to the breech face until the lug locks.
Thread protector or muzzle device back on clockwise, square and hand-tight to the maker's figure, bore checked for alignment.
Large end of the recoil spring assembly into the recess at the front of the slide, compressed, with the guide's rear centred on the barrel lug.
Slide and barrel onto the frame rails, all the way back, locked on the slide stop.
Takedown lever rotated upward to lock frame and slide, then release the slide forward.
Function-test the slide stop, trigger, magazine release and manual safety if fitted; if the optic came off, confirm its zero before the pistol is carried.
fncheck: Empty and reassembled: the takedown lever should sit flush and refuse to turn against a closed slide; the slide should run into battery under spring pressure and lock back on either ambidextrous stop; the trigger should reset audibly on a cycle; an empty magazine — 17 or 24 round — should drop free when the release is pressed; the thread protector or muzzle device should be square and tight with its bore in line; and on a Tactical fitted with the manual safety the levers should click into each position on their detent, bearing in mind FN's note that the safety cannot be engaged with the trigger held rearward.
